help.title: Help: setup with hub and voices
help.text.general:
A hub generates and holds the patterns of all voices. Each voice plays exactly one voice (bass, melody …) on its own track and gets its patterns from the hub. Slot and pattern changes are carried out by the whole group at the same bar. Only instances in the same process find each other.

How to set it up:

1. One variant for all instances: hub and voices must come from the same plug-in bundle (format and variant). Mixed variants do not connect.
2. One instance as the hub: choose the role “Hub”. The status line shows “Hub: n voices”.
3. One instance per voice as a voice: choose the role “Voice”, and next to it the voice (voice 1 = bass, voice 2 = melody). The voice shows “Connected to the hub”.
4. One instrument per track for the output of the voice. If the hub should stay silent, set “Output: none” on it.
5. Click “Generate” in the hub. In a voice the same button passes the request on to the hub.

Slot changes: a voice follows the slot of the hub (“Slot: follows the hub”). Automate the slot parameter in the hub. When bouncing a single track and when freezing, set the voice to “Slot: own” and automate its own slot parameter.

Mute works twice: if the hub switches “Mute n”, voice n is silent; if a voice switches its own mute, only that voice is silent.

If the hub is missing: the voices keep playing. The oldest voice offers “Become hub”; there is no silent takeover.

A saved pattern sounds the same after reloading, even if you change references later.

Drag & drop: the handle of each voice drags its .mid file (with the tempo of the DAW) into a clip.
help.text.live:
Ableton Live (VST3)

Setup per voice: one MIDI track with MidiMaid (hub or voice) and a second track with the synth. Live does not put a VST3 in front of a synth on the same track. Group both tracks of a voice into a group track (“Bass”, “Melody”).

Routing: on the synth track set “MIDI From” to the MidiMaid track of this voice, output “Post FX”.
Monitoring: synth track on “In”, otherwise it is silent unless it is armed.
Recording: arm the synth track and record. Live writes the MIDI after MidiMaid into a clip.
Freeze: Live freezes a track from its own clips, not from routed MIDI. Record first, then set the monitoring of the track to “Auto” or “Off” (with “In” Live refuses to freeze) and freeze.
Bounce of a track: set the voice to “Slot: own” and automate its slot parameter.
Arrangement: automate slot changes in the hub; a start in the middle of the arrangement takes the slot of the automation at that point.
Variant: all instances as VST3.

The hub track cannot be the master track: master and stereo out take no MIDI effects.
help.text.logic:
Logic Pro (AU, MIDI FX “MidiMaid MIDI”)

Setup: the hub sits as a MIDI FX on an instrument track (playing the bass there, for example), one voice each as a MIDI FX on the other instrument tracks.
Variant: all instances as “MidiMaid MIDI” (MIDI FX slot).
Recording: on every track with a voice switch on “Record MIDI to Track Here”. Logic then records the output after MidiMaid, otherwise no region is created.
Freeze and bounce: if hub and voices are on different tracks, the hub may not be active when a track is frozen. Set the voice to “Slot: own” and automate its slot parameter.
Arrangement: slot automation in the hub; recorded regions are normal MIDI.
help.text.other:
Bitwig: set the plug-in hosting to “By Plug-in” (not “Individually”). Hosts that run plug-ins in their own processes do not connect hub and voices; MidiMaid then shows “Hub not found” with a note about the sandbox.

Reaper and other hosts: the principle of the first tab applies. Check that all instances have the same format and run in the same process.

If instances do not find each other:
• Same variant and same format?
• Switch off the plug-in sandbox of the host.
• A second hub stays solo and shows “There is already a hub”.
